mainTopic: Chains of agents for a גט: changing the husband's instructions, the sick agent who appoints another through בית דין, and agents who cannot finish the job
overview: The amud opens by finishing a case. A husband told his agent to take an item from his wife and then give her the גט, but the agent reversed the order. רבי יוחנן rules the גט invalid even from the first agent, and ריש לקיש rules it valid even from the agent's agent. A new משנה teaches that an agent bringing a גט from overseas who becomes sick appoints another agent in בית דין, and the final agent only says "I am an agent of בית דין." From the words "final" and "agent of בית דין," the גמרא learns that a chain of agents is allowed and that each appointment must be made in בית דין. רבה says that in ארץ ישראל an agent can make several agents, and מר בר רב אשי rejects his father's view that the first agent's death cancels them all, since every agent acts on the husband's power. Two stories follow. In one, רב ספרא objects that an agent who was only sent to pass the גט on to אבא בר מניומי cannot transfer it. In the other, רבא lets an agent who was told to wait thirty days, and was then held back by circumstances, hand the גט over to his court. רבא defends that ruling against the worry that the husband may have made up with his wife, because she turned out to be only an ארוסה. The amud ends as רבא introduces a new question, which comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The agent reverses the husband's order
steps.stepSummary: The case: the husband said to take an item and then give the גט, but the agent gave the גט first and only then took the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband said: take an item from her and then give her the גט. The agent went and gave her the גט first, and only afterward took the item from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes describing a case where an agent did things in a different order than the husband told him. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband set a clear order: item first, then the גט. The agent reversed it. The question is whether changing the order means he stopped acting as the husband's agent.

keyTerms.meaning: The גט, the bill of divorce

phrases.english: Take an item from her
phrases.notes: These are the husband's words to his agent.

phrases.english: and then give her the bill of divorce;
and he went and gave her the bill of divorce,
and then took the item from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקוֹל מִינַּהּ חֵפֶץ וַהֲדַר הַב לַהּ גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is defined: the agent reversed the order the husband set.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about the agent and his agent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the גט is invalid even from the first agent, and certainly from his agent. ריש לקיש says it is valid even from the agent's agent, and certainly from the first agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says the גט is invalid when the first agent gives it, and even more so when that agent's own agent gives it. ריש לקיש says it is valid when the agent's agent gives it, and even more so when the first agent gives it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite rulings on the case from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that changing the husband's order cancels the agency, so even the first agent cannot make a valid גט. ריש לקיש is lenient at both levels. Each uses a כל שכן to show how far his ruling reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: His agent (here, the first agent's agent)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: invalid from the first agent, and certainly from his agent. ריש לקיש: valid from the agent's agent, and certainly from the first agent.
steps.confusionAlert: The two כל שכן statements run in opposite directions. רבי יוחנן reasons from the first agent down to his agent, while ריש לקיש reasons from the agent's agent up to the first agent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan invalidates it with him,
phrases.notes: "Him" means the first agent, when he gives the גט himself.

phrases.english: and all the more so with his agent,
and Reish Lakish validates it with his agent,
and all the more so with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings on the case defined in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן invalidates the גט at both levels. ריש לקיש validates it at both levels.

steps.title: The sick agent appoints another agent in court
steps.stepSummary: An agent bringing a גט from overseas who becomes sick appoints another agent in בית דין and makes the required declaration before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone is bringing a גט from overseas and becomes sick, he appoints another agent in בית דין and sends him. He himself says before the בית דין: "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what an agent bringing a גט from overseas does when he becomes sick and cannot finish the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט from overseas normally requires the agent to declare בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. Here the sick first agent makes that declaration in front of בית דין while appointing his replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: In court, in front of בית דין
It was written in my presence and signed in my presence

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who brings a bill of divorce from overseas,
and he became sick –
he appoints an agent in court and sends him,
and he says before them:
phrases.notes: "He" is the first, sick agent, speaking in front of the court.

phrases.english: "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the previous dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick agent appoints a new agent in בית דין and makes the declaration there himself.

steps.title: The final agent only says he is the court's agent
steps.stepSummary: The last agent does not repeat בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם. He only says: I am an agent of בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The final agent does not need to say "It was written and signed in my presence." Instead he says: "I am an agent of בית דין."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by explaining what the replacement agent says when he hands over the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration was already made in בית דין by the first agent, so the last agent does not repeat it. He only identifies himself as an agent of בית דין. The גמרא will soon draw proofs from two exact words here: "final" and "agent of בית דין."

keyTerms.meaning: The final agent, the one who actually delivers the גט

steps.whatToRemember: The first agent makes the declaration in בית דין. The final agent only says "I am an agent of בית דין."

phrases.english: and the final agent does not need to say
"It was written in my presence and signed in my presence,"

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר: שְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין אֲנִי.
phrases.english: rather he says: I am an agent of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final agent only needs to say he is an agent of בית דין.

steps.title: Can an agent's agent appoint yet another agent?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask אבימי to put a question to his father רבי אבהו: can a second agent appoint a third agent?
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to אבימי, son of רבי אבהו: Ask רבי אבהו whether an agent of an agent can appoint another agent, or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. If the second agent also becomes sick, can he pass the גט on to a third agent?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly allows the first agent to appoint a second. The open question is whether that second agent has the same power to appoint someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא, the discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages said
to Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu:
Ask of Rabbi Abbahu:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלִיחַ דְּשָׁלִיחַ מְשַׁוֵּי שָׁלִיחַ, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Can an agent of an agent appoint an agent, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a second agent can appoint a third agent for the גט.

steps.title: The word "final" proves there can be more agents
steps.stepSummary: No need to ask: the משנה says "the final agent," not "the second agent," which shows an agent's agent can appoint another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You don't need to ask this. Since the משנה says "the final agent," it is clear that an agent can keep appointing further agents.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered right away from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there could only ever be two agents, the משנה would have said "the second agent." Saying "the final agent" assumes there may be a longer chain, so a second agent can appoint a third.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לְכוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: You need not ask this,
since it teaches: "The final agent does not,"
phrases.notes: The point is that it says "final" and not "second."

phrases.english: by implication he can appoint an agent;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, an agent's agent can appoint another agent, as shown by the word "final."

steps.title: Must that appointment be made in court?
steps.stepSummary: The better question is whether the second agent must appoint the next agent in בית דין, or whether he may do it outside of בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if you want to ask, ask this: when the second agent appoints another agent, must he do it in בית דין, or may he do it even outside of בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: After setting aside the first question, the גמרא suggests a better question to ask instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states that the first appointment happens in בית דין. The new question is whether later appointments in the chain also need בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, when you ask, ask this

phrases.english: Rather, when you ask, ask this:
when he appoints an agent, must it be in court,
or even not in court?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the question that step 6 already answered with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a second agent's appointment of a third must take place in בית דין.

steps.title: "Agent of the court" proves it must be in court
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that this is also clear: the final agent says "I am an agent of בית דין," so he must have been appointed in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We have no question about this either. Since the משנה says the agent declares "I am an agent of בית דין," the appointment must be made in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer the new question from another phrase in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every final agent declares "I am an agent of בית דין." That declaration only makes sense if he was appointed in בית דין. So even later appointments in the chain must be made there.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no question about it

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's words teach two things: "final" shows a chain of agents is allowed, and "agent of בית דין" shows each appointment must be made in בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָא לָא מִבַּעְיָא לַן,
phrases.english: They said to him: We have no question about this,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָתָנֵי: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר ״שְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין אֲנִי״.
phrases.english: since it teaches: Rather, he says "I am an agent of the court."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The appointment must be made in בית דין, as shown by the words "I am an agent of בית דין."

steps.title: Second version: the חכמים ask only about בית דין
steps.stepSummary: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's version, the חכמים ask אבימי to ask רבי אבהו only one thing: must an agent's agent appoint the next agent in בית דין?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק taught the story differently. The חכמים told אבימי to ask his father רבי אבהו: when a second agent appoints another agent, must he do it in בית דין, or may he do it outside בית דין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same conversation. In this version, the question from the start is only about בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (steps 5-8), the question began with whether a second agent can appoint at all. Here the חכמים skip straight to the narrower question of בית דין. This sets up a new back-and-forth in which the roles are switched.

keyTerms.meaning: taught it this way (introduces another version)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same conversation from steps 5-8, told in a different version, and the details shift.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak taught it like this:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לַאֲבִימִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ,
phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Avimei, son of Rabbi Abahu,
Ask this of Rabbi Abahu:
An agent of an agent, when he appoints an agent,

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית דִּין, אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין?
phrases.english: must it be in court, or may it be outside of court?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the exchange in steps 5-8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must the second agent appoint the next agent in בית דין?

steps.title: אבימי suggests a more basic question
steps.stepSummary: אבימי answers: you should really be asking whether a second agent can appoint another agent at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You should be asking a more basic question: can a second agent appoint an agent at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The one being asked pushes back. He says the more basic question comes first: is a second agent even allowed to appoint someone?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of the first version. There, the חכמים raised the basic question and were told it was obvious. Here, the basic question is raised to the חכמים, and they will answer it.

phrases.english: He said to them: You should rather ask
whether he can appoint an agent at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיבְּעֵי לְכוּ אִי מְשַׁוֵּי שָׁלִיחַ בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Redirects the question in step 9 to a more basic one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a second agent appoint another agent at all?

steps.title: The חכמים: the basic question is already settled by the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the basic question is settled by the משנה's words 'the final agent.' Their real question is about בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We do not need to ask that. The משנה says 'the final agent,' which shows that an agent can appoint another agent. What we really want to know is whether it must be done in court or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים use the משנה's wording to show that an agent can appoint another agent. Then they repeat their real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the final agent' only makes sense if there can be a chain of several agents. So the basic question is already answered. Only the בית דין question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in the משנה
by inference, from this we learn

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן,
phrases.english: They said to him: This we do not need to ask,
as we learned: 'The final agent does not [need to say...]',
which shows that an agent can appoint an agent;
rather, what we are asking is:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית דִּין, אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין?
phrases.english: in court, or outside of court?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 and restates the question from step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, an agent can appoint another agent, as 'the final agent' in the משנה shows.

steps.title: The בית דין question is also settled by the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes back that this too is clear: the final agent says 'I am an agent of בית דין,' so he must have been appointed in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You do not need to ask this either, because the משנה teaches that the final agent says, 'I am an agent of בית דין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second question is also answered from the משנה's wording, the same way as in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone can only call himself 'an agent of בית דין' if he was appointed in בית דין. So the appointment must take place in court. Both versions reach the same conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: I am an agent of the court

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the משנה shows two things. A chain of agents is allowed, and each new agent must be appointed in בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָא נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לְכוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: This too you need not ask,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר ״שְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין אֲנִי״.
phrases.english: for it teaches: 'Rather, he says: I am an agent of the court.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לְכוּ, דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the בית דין question restated in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The appointment must be in בית דין, as shown by 'I am an agent of בית דין.'

steps.title: רבה: in ארץ ישראל an agent can make many agents
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that an agent in ארץ ישראל can create a chain of several agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: An agent in ארץ ישראל can make several agents.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts here. רבה says that inside ארץ ישראל an agent can pass the גט on through a chain of several agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case above was about a גט brought from outside ארץ ישראל, where the agent says בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם and the chain is made in בית דין. רבה's rule is about a גט inside ארץ ישראל. It is commonly explained that there this declaration is not needed, so the chain can be made even outside בית דין.

phrases.english: Rabba said: An agent in Eretz Yisrael
can make several agents.
phrases.notes: He means a chain: the agent appoints another, and that one can appoint another, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: chains of agents within ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within ארץ ישראל, an agent may appoint a chain of several agents.

steps.title: רב אשי: if the first agent dies, the whole chain is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that if the first agent dies, all the later agents lose their status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If the first agent dies, all of the agents are cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a rule to רבה's chain of agents: everything depends on the first agent staying alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי sees each agent as getting his power from the one who appointed him. So if the first link dies, the whole chain falls apart. The next step will challenge this.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִם מֵת רִאשׁוֹן –
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: If the first one dies,
they are all cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִם מֵת רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רבה's chain of agents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first agent's death cancels all the agents after him.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: all agents depend only on the husband
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rejects his father's ruling. All the agents act on the husband's power, so only the husband's death cancels them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: My father said this when he was young. Think about it: if the husband died, would any of the agents count for anything? Whose power are they all acting with? The husband's. If the husband is alive, they are all agents. If the husband is not alive, none of them are.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי's son rejects his father's rule. He says the first agent's death does not matter, because every agent is really the husband's agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that the husband's death ends all the agents, even though they are alive. That shows the agents depend on the husband, not on each other. So the first agent's death does not break the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: from his youth (said when he was young, so not his final view)
he is here / he is not here (alive or not alive)

steps.whatToRemember: In a chain of agents for a גט, every agent is the husband's agent. Only the husband's death cancels the agency, not the death of the first agent.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second agent is 'the first agent's agent' in a way that depends on the first agent's life. The first agent only passed along the husband's own appointment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic idea behind chains of agents: authority flows straight from the person who started it, not link by link.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
This ruling of my father is from his youth!
If the husband had died,
would there be any substance to them?!
All of them, from whose power do they come?
They come from the husband's power;
if the husband is alive, they all exist [as agents],
if the husband is not alive, none of them exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's ruling in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that the first agent's death cancels the later agents.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It treats the agents as depending on each other, when really they all depend only on the husband.

steps.title: The agent cannot find אבא בר מניומי
steps.stepSummary: A husband sends a גט with an agent who does not know the wife. He tells the agent to give it to אבא בר מניומי, but the agent cannot find him and comes to a group of sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man sent a גט to his wife. The agent said: I don't know her. The husband said: Give it to אבא בר מניומי, who knows her, and he will give it to her. The agent could not find אבא בר מניומי. He found רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפא and רבי יצחק נפחא, and רב ספרא was sitting with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a real-life case. It will test the rule from earlier about one agent appointing another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the husband's exact instruction: give the גט to אבא בר מניומי, and he will deliver it. That wording will decide whether this agent is a real divorce agent or only a messenger who carries the גט to אבא בר מניומי.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know her (I cannot recognize her)

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who sent a bill of divorce to his wife,
The agent said: I do not know her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל יַהֲבֵיהּ לְאַבָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go give it to Abba bar Minyumi,
for he knows her,
and let him go and give it to her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא וְלָא אַשְׁכַּח לְאַבָּא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי.
phrases.english: He came and did not find Abba bar Minyumi.

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא
phrases.english: He found Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa
and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
and Rav Safra was sitting with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real story that tests the earlier rule about agents appointing other agents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: the husband named אבא בר מניומי as the one who would deliver the גט, and he could not be found.

steps.title: The three sages tell the agent to pass his role to them
steps.stepSummary: The three sages tell the agent to hand over his agency to them, so they can give the גט to אבא בר מניומי when he arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Pass your role over to us. When אבא בר מניומי comes, we will give it to him, and he will go and give it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו, רבי חנינא בר פפא and רבי יצחק נפחא give a practical ruling. The agent should transfer his job to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They treat the agent as a real divorce agent who can appoint others. This fits רבה's rule from step 13 that an agent can create a chain of agents. The plan still ends with אבא בר מניומי delivering the גט, as the husband wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: Hand over your words, meaning pass on your agency

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מְסוֹר מִילָּךְ קַמֵּי דִּידַן,
phrases.english: They said to him: Hand over your words before us,
phrases.notes: He means: pass your job as the husband's agent over to us.

phrases.english: so that when Abba bar Minyumi comes
we will give it to him,
and he will go and give it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מְסוֹר מִילָּךְ קַמֵּי דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sages' ruling on the case set up in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The agent may transfer his agency to the sages, who will pass the גט on to אבא בר מניומי.

steps.title: רב ספרא objects that this agent cannot divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא points out that this agent was never given the power to divorce, so he cannot pass that power on. The sages are embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to them: But this is an agent who was not given the power to divorce! They were embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges the sages' ruling. They have no answer and feel ashamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent can only pass on what he himself holds. The husband only sent this agent to bring the גט to אבא בר מניומי. He never made him the one who divorces, so he has no divorce power to hand over to the sages.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent who was not given the power to divorce

steps.confusionAlert: רב ספרא is not arguing with רבה's rule that an agent can appoint another agent. He says that rule does not apply here, because this agent never had divorce power to begin with.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to them:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שְׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לְגֵירוּשִׁין הוּא!
phrases.english: But isn't he an agent who was not given the power to divorce!
They were embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא שְׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לְגֵירוּשִׁין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sages' ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sages' ruling that the agent may transfer his agency to them.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband sent this agent only to carry the גט to אבא בר מניומי, not to divorce. He has no divorce power, so he has none to pass on.

steps.title: רבא praises רב ספרא's win
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב ספרא defeated three ordained sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב ספרא beat three ordained sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא comments on the story. He says רב ספרא won the argument against three great ordained sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying this, רבא agrees that רב ספרא's objection was correct. The ruling of the three sages falls.

keyTerms.meaning: He struck them, meaning he beat them in argument

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rav Safra struck them down,
three ordained Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: קַפְּחִינְהוּ רַב סָפְרָא לִתְלָתָא רַבָּנַן סְמִוכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the exchange in step 18 and sides with רב ספרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא's objection was correct and defeated the three sages.

steps.title: רב אשי asks what the win was
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks how רב ספרא won. The husband never said that only אבא בר מניומי may deliver the גט and not the agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How did he beat them? Did the husband say to him, 'אבא בר מניומי and not you'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבא's praise. He argues that רב ספרא's objection does not really work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's reading, the husband made the agent a full divorce agent. He only added אבא בר מניומי as a helper because the agent did not know the wife. So the agent does have divorce power, he can pass it on as רבה taught, and the three sages were right.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: With what did he strike them?
Did the husband say to the agent:
'Abba bar Minyumi, and not you'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's claim in step 19 that רב ספרא won.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's statement and, through it, רב ספרא's objection.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The husband never ruled out the agent. Naming אבא בר מניומי was only a helpful option, so the agent was a real divorce agent.

steps.title: Second version: רבא says the win was a mistake
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא says רב ספרא defeated the three sages, but by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: רב ספרא beat three ordained sages, but it was a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבא's comment. Here רבא thinks the sages were actually right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This flips the first version. Now רבא is the one who doubts רב ספרא, while admitting the sages gave in to him.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say, introducing another version

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rava said:
Rav Safra struck down
three ordained Sages, mistakenly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רבא's comment from step 19, with the opposite view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא's objection was wrong, even though the sages gave in to it.

steps.title: רב אשי defends רב ספרא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks what the mistake was. By naming אבא בר מניומי, the husband meant that he should deliver the גט and not the agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What was the mistake? What did the husband tell him? 'אבא בר מניומי' means: and not you!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רבא's claim that רב ספרא was mistaken. He shows that רב ספרא was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב אשי reads the husband's words as excluding the agent. The agent was only a carrier, with no divorce power to pass to the sages. So רב ספרא's objection stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions turn on one question: did naming אבא בר מניומי mean 'and not you'? If yes, the agent had no divorce power and רב ספרא was right. If no, the agent was a real divorce agent and could pass his role to the sages.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What was the mistake?
What did the husband say to the agent?
'Abba bar Minyumi', and not you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's claim in step 21 that רב ספרא was mistaken.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's claim of a mistake and confirms רב ספרא's objection.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא overlooked that naming אבא בר מניומי excluded the agent from delivering the גט himself.

steps.title: A delayed גט and an agent who is held back
steps.stepSummary: A man sends a גט with a שליח and tells him to wait thirty days. Within the thirty days, the שליח is forced by circumstances he cannot control.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sent a גט to his wife. He told the שליח: Do not give it to her until thirty days have passed. Within the thirty days, something happened to the שליח that he could not control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new real-life case for the next steps. The שליח was told to wait thirty days, but something beyond his control will stop him from finishing the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things make this case hard. The שליח is not allowed to deliver the גט yet, and he cannot stay to deliver it later. The question is whether he can pass his mission on to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: he was forced by circumstances beyond his control

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לָהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ,
phrases.english: A certain man who sent a bill of divorce to his wife,
said to the agent:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּיתְּבֵיהּ נִיהֲלַהּ עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין.
phrases.english: Do not give it to her until thirty days.
He was forced by circumstances within the thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לָהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the story of רב ספרא and the three sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a שליח told to wait thirty days is forced to stop before the thirty days end.

steps.title: רבא lets the agent hand the mission to the court
steps.stepSummary: רבא compares the forced שליח to the משנה's sick שליח, who may appoint another. He tells the שליח to transfer his mission to the court. After thirty days the court will appoint a new שליח to deliver the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שליח came before רבא. רבא said: Why may a sick שליח appoint someone else? Because he is forced. This one is also forced. רבא told him: Hand your mission over to us. After thirty days we will appoint a שליח, and he will give the גט to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules that the forced שליח can pass his mission to רבא's court. The court will choose a new שליח once the thirty days are up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a sick שליח appoint another שליח because he is forced. רבא says the reason is being forced, not sickness itself, so any forced שליח gets the same rule. The court holds the mission until delivery is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: forced; held back by something beyond one's control
hand over your words, meaning pass on your mission

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's sick-agent rule depends on the reason behind it, being forced. So it can apply to other forced situations too.

phrases.english: He came before Rava.
Rava said: If he became sick, what is the reason?
Because he is forced.
This one too is forced.
phrases.notes: Both bracketed phrases mean 'he is forced.' The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions have the round-bracket words instead.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מְסוֹר מִילָּךְ קַמֵּי דִּידַן,
phrases.english: He said to him: Hand over your words before us,
so that after thirty days we will appoint an agent,
and he will give it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא, אָמַר רָבָא: חָלָה טַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's ruling on the case set up in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who is forced by circumstances, like a sick one, may transfer his mission. Here the court takes it and appoints a new שליח after thirty days.

steps.title: The rabbis object that this agent cannot divorce yet
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis challenge רבא. During the thirty days this שליח has no power to divorce, so he cannot pass that power on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis said to רבא: But he is a שליח who was not given the power to divorce!
steps.whatsHappening: The rabbis attack רבא's ruling. Right now this שליח is not allowed to deliver the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea רב ספרא used in step 18. A שליח can only pass on a power he actually has. During the thirty days, this שליח has no power to divorce at all.

keyTerms.meaning: an agent who was not given the power to divorce

phrases.english: The rabbis said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לְגֵירוּשִׁין הוּא!
phrases.english: But he is an agent who was not given the power to divorce!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: וְהָא שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לְגֵירוּשִׁין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the forced שליח may hand his mission to the court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שליח can only pass on a power he has. During the thirty days this שליח cannot divorce, so he has nothing to pass on.

steps.title: Future power counts as power now
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the שליח will be able to divorce after thirty days. Because of that, he already counts as a שליח who was given the power to divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Since after thirty days he can divorce, he is like a שליח who was given the power to divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. A power that is only delayed still counts as a real power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא separates two situations. In step 18 the שליח was never given the power to divorce. Here the power exists and is only waiting for the right time, so the שליח can pass it on.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not argue with רב ספרא's case. There the שליח never had the power to divorce. Here the power is only delayed.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דִּלְבָתַר תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין מָצֵי מְגָרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Since after thirty days he can divorce,
he is like an agent who was given the power to divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כֵּיוָן דִּלְבָתַר תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין מָצֵי מְגָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: a delayed power counts as a power already given.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שליח who cannot divorce yet is like one who was never given the power to divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he will be able to divorce after thirty days, he counts as a שליח given the power to divorce, and he may pass it on.

steps.title: A new worry: the husband may have made up with his wife
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: during the delay the husband may have made up with his wife and cancelled the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps the husband made up with her!
steps.whatsHappening: A new objection comes up against רבא's ruling. The thirty-day delay leaves time for the husband to change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attack is different from step 25. It is not about the שליח's power. It worries that during the delay the husband made peace with his wife and quietly cancelled the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: he was appeased; he made up and changed his mind
let us worry, let us take it into account

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he was appeased!
phrases.notes: He means the husband: maybe he made peace with his wife and cancelled the גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the power problem is solved, a new problem is raised against the same ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's plan to have a new שליח deliver the גט after thirty days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Over the delay the husband may have made up with his wife and cancelled the גט, so delivering it later could be worthless.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a conditional גט for twelve months
steps.stepSummary: To show that the worry is real, the גמרא quotes a משנה. A husband gives a גט that takes effect now if he does not return within twelve months, and he dies within that time. The גט is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn in a משנה: 'From now, if I do not come back from now until twelve months,' and he died within the twelve months, this is a valid גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof that we really do worry about the husband making up. First it quotes a משנה, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה too, there is a long gap before we know if the גט works. That makes it a good test case for the worry about making up. The next step shows how the גמרא dealt with that worry there.

keyTerms.meaning: didn't we learn in a משנה?
from now; the גט takes effect starting now

phrases.english: Didn't we learn in a mishna:
"From now, if I do not come back
from now until twelve months,"
and he died within twelve months,
this is a valid bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the support for the worry raised in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That the worry about the husband making up must be taken seriously.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a גט that takes effect now if the husband does not return within twelve months.

steps.title: That משנה needed a special answer to remove the worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reminds us that it asked on that משנה, 'Let us worry that he made up.' רבה בר רב הונא answered in the name of רב that the husband had declared his wife believed to say he did not return. Only that special statement removed the worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we asked on it: Let us worry that perhaps he made up! And רבה בר רב הונא said: This is what my father, my master, said in the name of רב: It is a case where he says, 'She is believed for me to say that I did not come back.'
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the proof. In the earlier משנה, the worry about making up was taken seriously and needed a special answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There, the husband made his wife believed, so he could not later claim he cancelled the גט. In our case the husband said nothing like that. So the worry that he made up stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: and we discussed it, we raised a question on it

steps.whatToRemember: The worry that the husband made up is real. In the twelve-month משנה it was removed only because the husband made his wife believed. Our case has no such statement.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
And let us worry that perhaps he was appeased!
And Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא מָרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: This is what my father, my master, said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: 'My father, my master' is רב הונא, the father of רבה בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: It is where he says: "She is believed against me
to say that I did not come back."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof started in step 28 by recalling how that משנה was explained.
steps.raayaObject: That we worry the husband may have made up during a delay.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier discussion of the twelve-month משנה. It needed רב's answer that the wife was declared believed, which shows the worry is real when there is no such statement.

steps.title: רבא's ruling is saved because the woman was only betrothed
steps.stepSummary: רבא was embarrassed by the challenge. Then it came out that the woman was an ארוסה. רבא says the worry that the husband made up with her applies only to a נשואה, not to an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was embarrassed. In the end it came out that she was only betrothed. רבא said: if the rabbis worried about this for a married woman, would they also worry about it for a betrothed woman?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא first feels he ruled wrongly. Then a new fact comes out, that the woman was only betrothed, and he uses it to defend his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in steps 27–29 was that the husband might have made up with his wife during the delay and cancelled the גט. The משנה about twelve months shows that worry for a נשואה, a wife who lives with him. רבא says we cannot carry that worry over to an ארוסה, so the challenge does not apply to his case.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter came to light, it turned out
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before living together
A fully married woman who lives with her husband

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back his ruling. He is showing that, in the actual case, the worry about making up never applied.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the worry about the husband making up depends on how close the couple is. It is stronger for a נשואה than for an ארוסה.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed. In the end the matter came to light
phrases.notes: The one embarrassed is רבא, because the challenge in step 29 seemed to prove his ruling wrong.

phrases.english: that she was a betrothed woman.
Rava said: If they said this about a married woman,
phrases.notes: "This" is the worry that the husband made up with his wife, from the משנה in steps 28–29.

phrases.english: would they say it about a betrothed woman?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in steps 27–29 by separating a נשואה from an ארוסה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the source deals with a נשואה, while רבא's case was an ארוסה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry that the husband made up with his wife applies to every wife, so רבא's ruling was wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry applies to a נשואה. It does not carry over to an ארוסה, so רבא's ruling stands.

steps.title: רבא introduces a question that is truly open
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is a question that he is certainly unsure about. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is certainly a question for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבא is about to raise a question he cannot settle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After defending his ruling, רבא admits that a related case really is in doubt. The word "certainly" tells us this is a real open question, not a challenge he can easily answer. The actual question comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a question for us, we are unsure

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is certainly a question for us:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the defense of his ruling, רבא opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated here. This line introduces a question that רבא considers truly unresolved, which comes next.
